wikidot5e:spell:conjure-vrock.effectSummary: Summon a vrock in a visible unoccupied space; it disappears at 0 HP or when the spell ends. At the start of each of its turns the DM secretly makes a Charisma check for you with a bonus equal to the consumed gem's gp value divided by 20; the DC starts at 10 and rises by 2 each round. While you succeed, it obeys your orders. On a failure, concentration is no longer required and you lose control; on its next turn it takes no action and telepathically offers to fight for treasure. The creature offering the most valuable gem commands it for 1d6 rounds, after which it offers again. If no treasure is offered before its next turn starts, it attacks the nearest creatures for 1d6 rounds and then returns to the Abyss. During casting you may draw a protective circle around your space using blood from an intelligent humanoid killed within the previous 24 hours; the vrock cannot cross or target anyone inside while the spell lasts.

wikidot5e:spell:conjure-woodland-beings.effectSummary: Summon fey into visible unoccupied spaces in range, choosing one CR 2-or-lower creature, two CR 1-or-lower, four CR 1/2-or-lower, or eight CR 1/4-or-lower. Each disappears at 0 HP or when the spell ends. They are friendly to you and your companions, share an initiative group with their own turns, and obey verbal commands without requiring your action; without commands they defend themselves but otherwise take no actions. The DM supplies their statistics. A 6th-level slot doubles the number summoned and an 8th-level slot triples it.

wikidot5e:spell:contact-other-plane.effectSummary: When casting, make a DC 15 Intelligence save. On a failure you take 6d6 psychic damage and become insane until you finish a long rest: you cannot take actions, understand speech, or read, and you can speak only gibberish; greater restoration ends this insanity. On a successful save, contact an extraplanar intelligence and ask up to five questions before the 1-minute duration ends. The DM answers each with one word such as yes, no, maybe, never, irrelevant, or unclear if the entity lacks the knowledge, but may use a short phrase when a one-word answer would be misleading.

wikidot5e:spell:contagion.effectSummary: Make a melee spell attack against a creature in reach; on a hit it becomes poisoned. At the end of each of its turns while poisoned, it makes a Constitution save. Three successes end the poison and the spell; three failures end the poison but inflict one chosen natural disease for the remainder of the 7-day duration, so effects that remove or mitigate disease work normally. Blinding Sickness: disadvantage on Wisdom checks and saves, and blinded. Filth Fever: disadvantage on Strength checks, Strength saves, and Strength-based attacks. Flesh Rot: disadvantage on Charisma checks and vulnerability to all damage. Mindfire: disadvantage on Intelligence checks and saves and, in combat, behavior as under confusion. Seizure: disadvantage on Dexterity checks, Dexterity saves, and Dexterity-based attacks. Slimy Doom: disadvantage on Constitution checks and saves, and whenever the creature takes damage it is stunned until the end of its next turn.

wikidot5e:spell:contingency.effectSummary: Choose another spell you can cast that is 5th level or lower, has a casting time of 1 action, and can target you. Cast it as part of contingency, expending both spell slots, but delay its effect until a circumstance you define occurs. The contingent spell triggers immediately after that circumstance first occurs, whether you want it to or not, and contingency then ends. The contingent spell affects only you even if it could normally target others. You can have only one contingency at a time; casting it again ends the previous one. The spell also ends if its required statuette is ever not on your person.

wikidot5e:spell:control-flames.effectSummary: Choose visible nonmagical flame in range that fits within a 5-foot cube and apply one option: instantly extend it 5 feet in one direction if fuel is present there; instantly extinguish the flames in the cube; for 1 hour double or halve its bright- and dim-light areas, change its color, or both; or for 1 hour create and animate simple shapes in the flames. You can have at most three noninstantaneous effects from repeated castings active at once and may dismiss one as an action.

wikidot5e:spell:control-water.effectSummary: Control freestanding water in a cube up to 100 feet on a side for the duration, choosing an effect when cast and using an action on later turns to repeat it or switch effects. Flood raises standing water by up to 20 feet, spilling over shores; in a large body it instead creates a 20-foot-high wave crossing the area, carrying Huge-or-smaller vehicles to the far side and giving each struck Huge-or-smaller vehicle a 25% capsize chance. Raised water persists until the spell ends or you change effects; a created wave repeats at the start of your next turn while Flood remains active. Part Water creates a trench across the area with walls of separated water; when the effect ends or changes, the trench refills over the next round. Redirect Flow makes flowing water move in any chosen direction, including over obstacles or uphill, while inside the area; once outside it resumes terrain-driven flow. Whirlpool requires water at least 50 feet square and 25 feet deep and creates a central vortex 5 feet wide at the base, up to 50 feet wide at the top, and 25 feet high. Creatures and objects in the water within 25 feet are pulled 10 feet toward it; a creature can swim away with a Strength (Athletics) check against your spell save DC. A creature entering the vortex for the first time on a turn or starting there makes a Strength save, taking 2d8 bludgeoning damage and becoming caught on a failure, or half damage without being caught on a success. A caught creature can use an action to swim away but makes that Athletics check with disadvantage. An object takes 2d8 bludgeoning damage the first time each turn it enters the vortex and again each round it remains there.

wikidot5e:spell:control-weather.effectSummary: Control weather within 5 miles while outdoors; moving where you lack a clear path to the sky ends the spell. You may change precipitation, temperature, and wind from current DM-determined conditions. Each change takes 1d4×10 minutes to take effect, after which you may change conditions again; when the spell ends, weather gradually returns to normal. Each adjustment moves a condition one stage up or down, and wind direction may also change. Precipitation stages: clear; light clouds; overcast or ground fog; rain, hail, or snow; torrential rain, driving hail, or blizzard. Temperature stages: unbearable heat; hot; warm; cool; cold; arctic cold. Wind stages: calm; moderate wind; strong wind; gale; storm.

wikidot5e:spell:control-winds.effectSummary: Control air in a visible 100-foot cube. Choose an effect when cast; on later turns use an action to switch effects, halt the current effect, or restart a halted one. Gusts creates horizontal wind in a chosen direction at calm, moderate, or strong intensity; moderate or strong wind imposes disadvantage on ranged weapon attacks passing through or targeting within the cube, and strong wind costs creatures moving against it 1 extra foot of movement per foot traveled. Downdraft creates strong downward wind, imposes the same ranged-attack disadvantage, and forces a flying creature entering the cube for the first time on a turn or starting there to make a Strength save or fall prone. Updraft makes creatures ending a fall in the cube take half falling damage and lets creatures in the cube jump vertically up to 10 feet higher than normal.

wikidot5e:spell:cordon-of-arrows.effectSummary: Plant four nonmagical arrows or bolts in the ground in range. Until the spell ends, whenever a creature other than you first comes within 30 feet of the ammunition on a turn or ends its turn there, one piece flies at it; the creature makes a Dexterity save, taking 1d6 piercing damage on a failure, and that ammunition is destroyed either way. The spell ends when no ammunition remains. When casting, designate any creatures the spell should ignore. Each slot level above 2nd lets the spell affect two additional pieces of ammunition.
